rows.round1_text: Salvador Dalí created this suite of illustrations in 1974 for a French luxury edition of Sigmund Freud's final 1939 book, *Moses and Monotheism*, published by Éditions Art & Valeur in Paris. Dalí drew upon Freud's provocative psychoanalytic thesis asserting that Moses was not Hebrew, but an Egyptian nobleman and follower of Akhenaten who was eventually murdered by his followers. Dalí had idolized Freud's theories on the subconscious since the 1920s and considered the text one of the psychoanalyst's most daring works. To create the edition, Dalí drew with a diamond stylus onto printing plates, combining lithography and drypoint etching directly onto sheets of sheepskin.
